classification.difficultyReason: Extract the two triangles from the crossing-line grid and justify their correspondence using a half-turn with enlargement, or parallel bases and vertically opposite angles. Comparing base and height alone needs this geometric justification to establish similarity.

content.prompt: Whitney says triangle A and B are similar. Do you agree? Why?

spec.description: Six-by-six square grid with opposing triangles sharing the crossing of two straight segments. The grid template cannot express the crossing segments and internal triangle labels, so the complete figure uses TikZ.
spec.mathematics: In source coordinates measured rightwards and downwards, segments join (0,0) to (6,6) and (3,0) to (0,6), crossing at (2,2). Triangle A has vertices (0,0), (3,0), (2,2); triangle B has vertices (0,6), (6,6), (2,2). Their bases lie on opposite grid boundaries.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied grid, triangle boundaries and labels A and B are visible.

answer.short: Yes. B has double the base and double the height of A.
answer.worked: Yes. A has base 3 grid units and height 2 grid units; B has base 6 grid units and height 4 grid units. Enlarging A by scale factor 2 about the crossing point and rotating it through $180^\circ$ gives B. Corresponding sides are therefore in the same ratio and corresponding angles are equal.
